knowledge:
- key_parameters: junc.type=In spliceGene, set to "score" to calculate 3S scores or "count" to obtain raw junction read counts ;; cores=In BMfinder, specifies the number of threads/cores to use for parallel processing ;; gene.select=In spliceGenome, a vector of gene IDs to select for genome-wide calculation (set to NA for all) ;; intron.select=In spliceGenome, a vector of intron IDs to select for genome-wide calculation (set to NA for all) ;; genes=In getGeneinfo, a character vector of gene IDs to retrieve information for
- alternatives: The Sushi package (specifically plotBedgraph and plotGenes) is mentioned for plotting depth and gene structures, which serves as the underlying engine for VaSP's deprecated visualization functions.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have short-read RNA-seq data mapped with HISAT2, assembled with StringTie, and compiled into a Ballgown object, and you want to quantify alternative splicing (3S scores) and identify genotype-specific splicing (GSS) or bimodal splicing distribution features across a population.
- pitfalls: The visualizing function splicePlot is deprecated and removed because its dependency package Sushi is deprecated. BMfinder will output a warning if the sample size is less than 30, indicating the results should be further tested. spliceGene can only calculate scores for one gene at a time; spliceGenome must be used for genome-wide calculations. The ballgown package itself is deprecated in Bioconductor version 3.24.

workflows.name: splicing_quantification_and_gss_discovery
workflows.intent: Calculate Single Splicing Strength (3S) scores and identify genotype-specific splicing (GSS) events from a Ballgown object.
input: rice.bg (Ballgown object containing transcript assembly and expression information)
Sample_027.bam (BAM file for extracting read depth)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate 3S scores or junction counts for a specific gene using spliceGene, or genome-wide using spliceGenome. ;; 2. Identify bimodal distribution features (GSS events) using BMfinder. ;; 3. Extract genomic coordinates of the identified GSS introns using structure. ;; 4. Extract read depth from BAM files using getDepth and gene information using getGeneinfo.
workflows.code:
library(VaSP)
data(rice.bg)
score<-spliceGene(rice.bg, gene="MSTRG.183", junc.type = "score")
count <- spliceGene(rice.bg, "MSTRG.183", junc.type = "count")
gss <- BMfinder(score, cores = 1)
gss_intron<-structure(rice.bg)$intron
(gss_intron<-gss_intron[gss_intron$id%in%rownames(gss)])
range(gss_intron)
splice <- spliceGenome(rice.bg, gene.select = NA, intron.select = NA)
path <- system.file("extdata", package = "VaSP")
bam_files <- list.files(path, "*.bam$")
depth <- getDepth(file.path(path, bam_files[1]), "Chr1", start = 1171800, end = 1179400)
gene_id <- c("MSTRG.181", "MSTRG.182", "MSTRG.183")
geneinfo <- getGeneinfo(genes = gene_id, rice.bg)
